edges.effect_quant: Different designs and subgroups point in different directions, so a single pooled estimate is not the right way to read this edge.
edges.mechanism: The proposed route is retrograde migration of talc particles with chronic ovarian inflammation, but the biological and epidemiologic case remains debated, which is why this edge is often contentious.
edges.summary: For ovarian cancer, the most useful starting point is the 2003 Huncharek meta analysis in Anticancer Res. It found that perineal cosmetic talc use produces mixed findings across studies, and the follow-on evidence is broadly consistent even when absolute benefit or harm is modest.
edges.caveats: This is a contested edge. Exposure measurement, confounding, and publication-era effects all matter, so confidence should stay low until cleaner data accumulate.

evidence.notes: Perineal application of cosmetic talc and risk of invasive epithelial ovarian cancer: a meta-analysis of 11,933 subjects from sixteen observational studies.
